live.instructions: MCP reporting and workflow metric date ranges use yyyy-MM-dd and include both startDate and endDate, with at most 95 calendar days per range. For longer read-only reports, split into non-overlapping windows: endDate = startDate plus 94 days, capped at the requested end date; the next startDate is the previous endDate plus 1 day. Apply the same limit independently to comparison ranges. Do not average ratios such as ACOS or ROAS across windows; recompute them from summed base metrics. Do not automatically split advertising write plans or metric-based selectors; obtain a supported analysis window from the user. Keyword ranking trends have separate limits: DAILY supports up to 90 inclusive days and RAW up to 31 inclusive days. For keyword ranking trends, use these interval-specific limits when splitting read-only reports. This reporting limit does not apply to campaign scheduling dates. Use the advertised operation-specific preparation tool to create an immutable Amazon Ads plan. Review it with the customer, confirm it through confirm_workflow_plan, then use the matching operation-specific execution tool. For dependent Campaign, Ad Group, Product Ad, and targeting creation, prepare_workflow_draft and continue_workflow_draft preserve dependencies. Each returned atomic plan requires its own review and confirmation. For advertising, choose the execution tool from the plan's workflowType. Keyword tracking exposes separate creation, status changes, and competitor replacement tools; use the returned nextApplyTool for its exact approved operation group. An execution may return the next-stage preview but never confirms the next plan. Follow returned nextActions and ask only for missing business inputs; do not replace a concrete next step with a generic offer to continue.

tools.name: continue_workflow_draft
tools.description: Resumes a READY AD_STRUCTURE_CREATE draft from persisted server state. This call may query Amazon Ads for keyword or ASIN candidates and suggested bids, including candidates not yet created in the account, or reuse saved recommendations. It persists workflow progress and decisions. It reconciles the last atomic plan, retains successful Amazon IDs, and prepares exactly the next Campaign, Ad Group, Product Ad, automatic-target bid, or Targeting plan. All Campaigns are prepared together, then all Ad Groups, then all Product Ads across every ad group in one multi-group plan; the Product Ad plan is completed before any targeting recommendation or bid decision can pause another structure. It never confirms or applies a write plan. For AUTO ad groups it persists the selected bid mode with the created adGroupId, synchronizes the four Amazon-created targets, obtains suggested bids when selected, and returns a separately confirmable AD_TARGETING_CHANGE plan. Partial writes retry only failed items. A 429 suggestion read includes per-target evidence; ambiguous create results require reconciliation and are never retried. For MANUAL ad groups without supplied positive targeting, it waits until Product Ads exist, persists Amazon candidates only for the recorded KEYWORD or ASIN TARGET family, accepts customer selection by candidateRef, obtains suggested or custom bids, accepts explicit customCandidates when recommendations are absent or rejected, and prepares separately confirmable Targeting plans. It accepts at most 100 selected candidates per ad group and reuses the exact suggested bids already shown to the customer. Once every manual decision is ready, it combines all MANUAL positive targeting groups into one batch plan, then combines all configured negative targeting across AUTO and MANUAL groups into one separate batch plan. AUTO-only drafts skip MANUAL processing and MANUAL-only drafts skip AUTO processing. When a plan is returned, pass applyContinuation unchanged to the matching operation-specific execution tool so a successful write automatically returns the next stage preview without asking the customer to advance. After an AUTO bid write, immediately present the returned MANUAL targeting preview or selection action in the same response when manual groups remain.
tools.title: Continue workflow draft

manualTargetingDecisions.description: Optional decisions keyed by a deferred MANUAL ad-group clientRef. First submit up to 100 candidateRef values returned by MANUAL_TARGETING_SELECTION_REQUIRED, or add customer-approved customCandidates when recommendations are absent or rejected. All candidates for one ad group must be KEYWORD or TARGET, never both; use separate manual Campaign/Ad Group structures when both targeting families are required. Then choose AMAZON_SUGGESTED, or CUSTOM with one bid for every selected candidateRef. Selection and bid choice may be submitted together when the customer already requested suggested bids.

candidateRef.description: Selected candidateRef receiving this custom bid.

customCandidates.description: Customer-approved explicit keywords or ASIN targets for this already created ad group. All custom and selected candidates for an ad group must belong to exactly one positive targeting family; create a separate manual Campaign/Ad Group structure to use the other family. Every supplied custom candidate is automatically selected and receives the stable candidateRef custom:<clientRef>. Use that candidateRef in CUSTOM bids. This also lets the workflow continue when Amazon returns no recommendations or the customer rejects them.

clientRef.description: Stable client reference unique among this ad group's custom candidates.

asin.description: Required 10-character ASIN for TARGET and omitted for KEYWORD.

matchType.description: Required for KEYWORD and omitted for TARGET.

keywordText.description: Required for KEYWORD and omitted for TARGET.

bidMode.description: Bid source for all selected candidates.

targetingFamily.description: KEYWORD or TARGET for a legacy deferred manual ad group that did not persist manualTargetingFamily in its draft. New drafts record the family before execution.

selectedCandidateRefs.description: Select candidates from exactly one positive targeting family for this ad group: all KEYWORD or all TARGET. To use both families, create separate manual Campaign/Ad Group structures.

items.description: Stable candidateRef returned by the persisted recommendation action.

expectedDraftVersion.description: Latest draftVersion used for optimistic locking and safe recovery.

automaticTargetBidDecisions.description: Optional decisions keyed by AUTO ad-group clientRef, used after a DECIDE_LATER or incomplete recommendation result.

tools.name: prepare_workflow_draft
tools.description: Creates or incrementally updates an AD_STRUCTURE_CREATE draft. Collect the Sponsored Products Campaign/Ad Group/Product Ad structure and any targeting the customer already supplied. One MANUAL ad group can contain only one positive targeting family: KEYWORD or ASIN TARGET. If positive targeting is omitted, collect manualTargetingFamily=KEYWORD|TARGET before execution. If the customer wants both, model separate manual Campaign/Ad Group structures from the start and assign one family to each; never put both into one ad group. Every ad group needs a negative-targeting decision: supplied allowed negative items automatically record negativeTargetingMode=CONFIGURED; when none are supplied, recommend negatives and ask the customer to choose CONFIGURED or NONE. AUTO permits both negative keywords and negative ASINs; a MANUAL KEYWORD group permits only negative keywords, and a MANUAL TARGET group permits only negative ASINs. Continuation prepares all Campaigns together, then all Ad Groups, then all Product Ads across every ad group in one multi-group plan before any AUTO bid decision or MANUAL recommendation can pause the draft. After all Product Ads exist, continuation queries and persists Amazon recommendations only for each manual ad group's recorded family, asks the customer to choose up to 100 candidates, obtains suggested or custom bids, then combines all ready MANUAL positive targeting into one Targeting batch plan. It subsequently combines every configured negative targeting item across AUTO and MANUAL structures into one separate negative Targeting batch plan. AUTO-only drafts skip the MANUAL stage and MANUAL-only drafts skip the AUTO stage. If recommendations are absent or rejected, submit customer-approved customCandidates of the same family to the continuation; do not recreate the already-created structure. For every AUTO ad group, explain that Amazon creates exactly four targets after the ad group exists and record automaticTargetBidding.mode as KEEP_DEFAULT, AMAZON_SUGGESTED, CUSTOM, or DECIDE_LATER; CUSTOM requires all four official theme bids. Never model those themes as manually created targets. Every supplied nested entity requires a stable clientRef. Updating requires draftId and expectedDraftVersion; arrays merge by clientRef and remove only through removeClientRefs. When the draft is READY, call continue_workflow_draft. The server then persists the current atomic plan, created Amazon IDs, recommendation choices, and bid choice so later calls safely resume. Recommendation 429 responses are recoverable and do not create a write plan. During draft collection, accept syntactically valid SKU/ASIN values without querying Inventory or Listings; production Product Ad plan preparation performs product resolution.

tools.name: query_advertising_bid_recommendations
tools.description: Read-only POST that returns current Amazon suggested bids and bid ranges for 1 to 100 Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, or Sponsored Display targeting items. For an existing keyword or target, provide targetingType and targetingId only. For a candidate that has not been created, first create its ad group, then provide targetingType, adGroupId, and targeting; this operation does not create the candidate. The server resolves the advertising product, Campaign, and Ad Group from synchronized data, so clients do not provide adProduct or campaignId. Compatible items in the same product, Campaign, Ad Group, and targeting type are combined into one Amazon recommendation request. Successful group responses are cached briefly and reused for identical requests. If a group is rate-limited, earlier successful groups are preserved, later groups of the same advertising product are not sent, and other advertising products continue. Retry only retryItemIndexes after retryAfterSeconds; do not immediately repeat the complete request when requestFingerprint is unchanged. Rate-limited and deliberately skipped unfinished items both retain the backward-compatible TOO_MANY_REQUESTS code; details distinguish them. Retrieves bid recommendations from Amazon Ads using the authorized advertising profile, or reuses cached recommendation results. Supports existing targets and supplied keyword or product targeting candidates that have not been created in the advertising account. This is a read-only tool: it neither creates targeting entities nor applies the returned bid. Use it when a bid decision needs Amazon's recommendation; historical CPC is not a suggested bid. Never repeat an unchanged request in the same assistant turn. Reuse successful items and the same requestFingerprint response. On TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, wait at least retryAfterSeconds and call this tool again with only retryItemIndexes.

tools.name: query_advertising_target_recommendations
tools.description: Read-only POST that returns Amazon-recommended keyword or ASIN targeting candidates before targeting entities are created. Supply exactly one source: adGroupId, or asins with adProduct. With adGroupId, the server resolves Campaign, advertising product, advertised ASINs, Sponsored Brands creative context, and Sponsored Display tactic from synchronized data. Sponsored Products supports KEYWORD and TARGET recommendations, Sponsored Brands supports KEYWORD and TARGET recommendations, and Sponsored Display supports TARGET recommendations only. Sponsored Display ASIN product recommendations require tactic T00020 because Amazon v3.3 does not support PRODUCT recommendations for T00030. TARGET currently means recommended ASIN product targets; category, brand, and audience recommendations are not included. Sponsored Products and Sponsored Brands TARGET responses can return nextToken for the next page. Pass that token back unchanged while keeping the original recommendation context. If Amazon rate-limits any page, the server does not retry and returns HTTP 429 with code TOO_MANY_REQUESTS; retain previously received items and retry only the failed page with the same nextToken. Each returned targeting object can be copied into a candidate bid-recommendation item together with the created adGroupId and targetingType, then used to create the selected target. This operation does not create or update advertising entities. Recommendations are retrieved from the Amazon Ads recommendation APIs using the authorized advertising profile and supplied context. Returned candidates are not limited to targeting entities already present in the user's advertising account. Use this tool first when the customer has not selected targeting candidates, then pass selected targeting objects to query_advertising_bid_recommendations before creation.

tools.name: query_keyword_rank_trackers
tools.description: One trackingScope per request: PARENT (default) uses parentAsin and tracks the family; CHILD uses asin and tracks only that exact variation, excluding siblings. The server resolves its parent. For tracker lists use parentAsins with PARENT or asins with CHILD. Query, ADD, RESUME, REMOVE and SET_COMPETITORS must preserve the same scope and target. Both OWN_PRODUCT and independent COMPETITOR support CHILD. For OWN_PRODUCT associations, PARENT competitorAsins are parent/standalone ASINs while CHILD competitorAsins are exact variation ASINs. includeCompetitors compares the same scope. Account capabilities and notices are returned even for empty results. Check advertisingRankTracking before interpreting advertising ranks or offering advertising tracking. False means unsupported, not a missing match; never promise advertising ranks or silently substitute organic tracking for an explicit advertising-rank request. This applies to own products, independent competitors, and associated competitors. Returns keyword rank tracking configuration across authorized stores. Groups top-level items by storeId and the selected tracking target with nested keywords, and may include PENDING_KEYWORDS parents. Each tracking record has a stable trackingId and its own ACTIVE or PAUSED state. PAUSED means the system stopped tracking due to package expiry or restrictions; it is not a customer pause action. Restore it with RESUME only when package access and quota permit. Returns all matching configuration without pagination. Product title and imageUrl are included when available. Latest rankings are not included; use query_keyword_rank_trends with storeId, parentAsin and keywords to retrieve rankings. This tool does not return Search Volume or calculate rank changes. Query query_account_usages with resources=[KEYWORD_RANK_TRACKING_KEYWORDS] for account quota; list counts are not quota usage. One product type per request: OWN_PRODUCT (default) or independent COMPETITOR. Call separately for each type; ALL and mixed selections are not supported. Competitors share account-wide marketplace/keyword quota with owned products. To create tracking use prepare_keyword_rank_tracking_creation; to resume or archive existing keywords use prepare_keyword_rank_tracking_changes; to replace associated competitors use prepare_keyword_rank_competitor_replacement. Follow each published schema and obtain explicit customer confirmation before its matching apply tool. Preserve the returned trackingScope: PARENT uses parentAsin; CHILD uses asin. Never substitute the parent when a customer requests one child.

tools.name: query_keyword_rank_trends
tools.description: One trackingScope per request: PARENT (default) uses parentAsin and tracks the family; CHILD uses asin and tracks only that exact variation, excluding siblings. The server resolves its parent. For tracker lists use parentAsins with PARENT or asins with CHILD. Query, ADD, RESUME, REMOVE and SET_COMPETITORS must preserve the same scope and target. Both OWN_PRODUCT and independent COMPETITOR support CHILD. For OWN_PRODUCT associations, PARENT competitorAsins are parent/standalone ASINs while CHILD competitorAsins are exact variation ASINs. includeCompetitors compares the same scope. Account capabilities and notices are returned even for empty results. Check advertisingRankTracking before interpreting advertising ranks or offering advertising tracking. False means unsupported, not a missing match; never promise advertising ranks or silently substitute organic tracking for an explicit advertising-rank request. This applies to own products, independent competitors, and associated competitors. First discover tracked products and keywords with query_keyword_rank_trackers (all matching configuration is returned without pagination). For DAILY, provide one storeId, one scope-specific ASIN and 1 to 10 exact tracked keywords, plus startDate/endDate (up to 90 inclusive marketplace-local days). All requested daily points return in one response; there is no offset/limit pagination. Split more than 10 keywords into separate requests. Each day keeps the last actual observation; absent days are not synthesized. Equal-time ties use child ASIN descending, current source first, then ID descending, not best rank. RAW uses the same storeId and scope-specific ASIN with exactly one keyword, supports 31 inclusive days, and uses offset and limit (default and maximum 100) over observation points; increase offset by limit until fewer than limit points are returned. RAW preserves distinct child ASINs and prefers current records over archived copies. One product type per request: OWN_PRODUCT (default) or independent COMPETITOR. Call separately for each type; ALL and mixed selections are not supported. Competitors share account-wide marketplace/keyword quota with owned products. MCP reporting and workflow metric date ranges use yyyy-MM-dd and include both startDate and endDate, with at most 95 calendar days per range. For longer read-only reports, split into non-overlapping windows: endDate = startDate plus 94 days, capped at the requested end date; the next startDate is the previous endDate plus 1 day. Apply the same limit independently to comparison ranges. Do not average ratios such as ACOS or ROAS across windows; recompute them from summed base metrics. Do not automatically split advertising write plans or metric-based selectors; obtain a supported analysis window from the user. Keyword ranking trends have separate limits: DAILY supports up to 90 inclusive days and RAW up to 31 inclusive days. For keyword ranking trends, use these interval-specific limits when splitting read-only reports. This reporting limit does not apply to campaign scheduling dates.

tools.name: query_sales
tools.description: Returns sales summaries, daily sales summaries, SKU sales, or daily SKU sales for a business date range. The range is inclusive and each request may contain at most 95 calendar days. When splitting a longer range, set endDate to startDate plus 94 days, then start the next range at the previous endDate plus 1 day; a 95-day difference between startDate and endDate would contain 96 inclusive days and is invalid. MCP reporting and workflow metric date ranges use yyyy-MM-dd and include both startDate and endDate, with at most 95 calendar days per range. For longer read-only reports, split into non-overlapping windows: endDate = startDate plus 94 days, capped at the requested end date; the next startDate is the previous endDate plus 1 day. Apply the same limit independently to comparison ranges. Do not average ratios such as ACOS or ROAS across windows; recompute them from summed base metrics. Do not automatically split advertising write plans or metric-based selectors; obtain a supported analysis window from the user. Keyword ranking trends have separate limits: DAILY supports up to 90 inclusive days and RAW up to 31 inclusive days. For keyword ranking trends, use these interval-specific limits when splitting read-only reports. This reporting limit does not apply to campaign scheduling dates.

tools.name: query_sales_orders
tools.description: Returns one store's sales orders with all order items in descending purchase time. Uses a UTC start-inclusive, end-exclusive window of at most 31 days. Excludes canceled, non-Amazon and replacement orders. SKU and promotion filters select whole orders. The time window always filters purchasedAt (order purchase time), never refund or return event time. REFUND means the order currently has a refund flag in the latest synchronized data; it does not necessarily mean a full refund or a physical return. An order purchased in July and refunded in September matches a July purchase window with REFUND, but not a September purchase window. Historical results may change after later refunds are synchronized. This endpoint cannot answer which refunds or returns occurred during a period. Amounts may be estimated; amounts after promotion are not settlement proceeds. Missing prices or order currency produce null amounts. Use this endpoint for individual orders and their items; use Sales reports for aggregated sales metrics and Profit reports for profit, refunds and costs. Order amount sums are not guaranteed to reconcile with report sales or netSales. Returns no total count. Offset pagination is not a snapshot; deduplicate by storeId and orderId when collecting changing data.

tools.description: Executes only a confirmed AD_AD_GROUP_CHANGE plan on the authorized Amazon Ads account. Changes ad-group default bids, states, or names. Requires the plan's one-time confirmation receipt and an idempotency key. A linked structure draft may automatically prepare the next preview without confirming or executing it. inputSchema.description: Execute only the reviewed and confirmed plan. After a successful write, present the returned next-stage preview without asking permission merely to advance stages; each next write plan still requires its own confirmation. After an automatic-target bid plan succeeds, present any returned MANUAL positive-targeting batch preview or selection action in the same response; do not stop at the four successful automatic bids while manual groups remain. Standalone Campaign, Ad Group, and Product Ad creation results return ordered nextActions. Present or execute the immediate read/plan-preparation action when its inputs are already known, rather than only offering to continue.

planId.description: Confirmed immutable workflow plan ID. If this call times out or disconnects, do not prepare a replacement plan: query get_workflow_plan, or retry this exact plan with the same idempotency key. An INDETERMINATE item means Amazon may have accepted the write and must be reconciled before any retry.

applyContinuation.description: For atomic plans belonging to an AD_STRUCTURE_CREATE draft. Pass the applyContinuation object returned by continue_workflow_draft or the previous apply result unchanged with its current plan. After the approved write finishes, the server prepares the next-stage preview without confirming or executing it. If omitted, continuation may still be recovered from the active linked plan. Review Sandbox skips automatic continuation.

confirmationReceipt.description: One-time receipt returned by confirm_workflow_plan for this exact plan. A receipt for the current plan does not confirm subsequent plans.

idempotencyKey.description: Client-generated key unique to this plan. Generate a new key for every newly prepared plan; include the planId or another random value. Reuse the exact key only when retrying apply for this same plan; never reuse it for a newly prepared plan.

tools.name: continue_workflow_draft
tools.description: Resumes a READY AD_STRUCTURE_CREATE draft from persisted server state. This call may query Amazon Ads for keyword or ASIN candidates and suggested bids, including candidates not yet created in the account, or reuse saved recommendations. It persists workflow progress and decisions. It reconciles the last atomic plan, retains successful Amazon IDs, and prepares exactly the next Campaign, Ad Group, Product Ad, automatic-target bid, or Targeting plan. All Campaigns are prepared together, then all Ad Groups, then all Product Ads across every ad group in one multi-group plan; the Product Ad plan is completed before any targeting recommendation or bid decision can pause another structure. It never confirms or applies a write plan. For AUTO ad groups it persists the selected bid mode with the created adGroupId, synchronizes the four Amazon-created targets, obtains suggested bids when selected, and returns a separately confirmable AD_TARGETING_CHANGE plan. Partial writes retry only failed items. A 429 suggestion read includes per-target evidence; ambiguous create results require reconciliation and are never retried. For MANUAL ad groups without supplied positive targeting, it waits until Product Ads exist, persists Amazon candidates only for the recorded KEYWORD or ASIN TARGET family, accepts customer selection by candidateRef, obtains suggested or custom bids, accepts explicit customCandidates when recommendations are absent or rejected, and prepares separately confirmable Targeting plans. It accepts at most 100 selected candidates per ad group and reuses the exact suggested bids already shown to the customer. Once every manual decision is ready, it combines all MANUAL positive targeting groups into one batch plan, then combines all configured negative targeting across AUTO and MANUAL groups into one separate batch plan. AUTO-only drafts skip MANUAL processing and MANUAL-only drafts skip AUTO processing. When a plan is returned, pass applyContinuation unchanged to the matching operation-specific execution tool so a successful write automatically returns the next stage preview without asking the customer to advance. After an AUTO bid write, immediately present the returned MANUAL targeting preview or selection action in the same response when manual groups remain.
tools.title: Continue workflow draft

manualTargetingDecisions.description: Optional decisions keyed by a deferred MANUAL ad-group clientRef. First submit up to 100 candidateRef values returned by MANUAL_TARGETING_SELECTION_REQUIRED, or add customer-approved customCandidates when recommendations are absent or rejected. All candidates for one ad group must be KEYWORD or TARGET, never both; use separate manual Campaign/Ad Group structures when both targeting families are required. Then choose AMAZON_SUGGESTED, or CUSTOM with one bid for every selected candidateRef. Selection and bid choice may be submitted together when the customer already requested suggested bids.

candidateRef.description: Selected candidateRef receiving this custom bid.

customCandidates.description: Customer-approved explicit keywords or ASIN targets for this already created ad group. All custom and selected candidates for an ad group must belong to exactly one positive targeting family; create a separate manual Campaign/Ad Group structure to use the other family. Every supplied custom candidate is automatically selected and receives the stable candidateRef custom:<clientRef>. Use that candidateRef in CUSTOM bids. This also lets the workflow continue when Amazon returns no recommendations or the customer rejects them.

clientRef.description: Stable client reference unique among this ad group's custom candidates.

asin.description: Required 10-character ASIN for TARGET and omitted for KEYWORD.

matchType.description: Required for KEYWORD and omitted for TARGET.

keywordText.description: Required for KEYWORD and omitted for TARGET.

bidMode.description: Bid source for all selected candidates.

targetingFamily.description: KEYWORD or TARGET for a legacy deferred manual ad group that did not persist manualTargetingFamily in its draft. New drafts record the family before execution.

tools.name: diagnose_ad_efficiency
tools.description: Diagnoses advertising efficiency with read-only advertising metrics for one store and business date range. MCP reporting and workflow metric date ranges use yyyy-MM-dd and include both startDate and endDate, with at most 95 calendar days per range. For longer read-only reports, split into non-overlapping windows: endDate = startDate plus 94 days, capped at the requested end date; the next startDate is the previous endDate plus 1 day. Apply the same limit independently to comparison ranges. Do not average ratios such as ACOS or ROAS across windows; recompute them from summed base metrics. Do not automatically split advertising write plans or metric-based selectors; obtain a supported analysis window from the user. Keyword ranking trends have separate limits: DAILY supports up to 90 inclusive days and RAW up to 31 inclusive days. For keyword ranking trends, use these interval-specific limits when splitting read-only reports. This reporting limit does not apply to campaign scheduling dates.

tools.name: prepare_workflow_draft
tools.description: Creates or incrementally updates an AD_STRUCTURE_CREATE draft. Collect the Sponsored Products Campaign/Ad Group/Product Ad structure and any targeting the customer already supplied. One MANUAL ad group can contain only one positive targeting family: KEYWORD or ASIN TARGET. If positive targeting is omitted, collect manualTargetingFamily=KEYWORD|TARGET before execution. If the customer wants both, model separate manual Campaign/Ad Group structures from the start and assign one family to each; never put both into one ad group. Every ad group needs a negative-targeting decision: supplied allowed negative items automatically record negativeTargetingMode=CONFIGURED; when none are supplied, recommend negatives and ask the customer to choose CONFIGURED or NONE. AUTO permits both negative keywords and negative ASINs; a MANUAL KEYWORD group permits only negative keywords, and a MANUAL TARGET group permits only negative ASINs. Continuation prepares all Campaigns together, then all Ad Groups, then all Product Ads across every ad group in one multi-group plan before any AUTO bid decision or MANUAL recommendation can pause the draft. After all Product Ads exist, continuation queries and persists Amazon recommendations only for each manual ad group's recorded family, asks the customer to choose up to 100 candidates, obtains suggested or custom bids, then combines all ready MANUAL positive targeting into one Targeting batch plan. It subsequently combines every configured negative targeting item across AUTO and MANUAL structures into one separate negative Targeting batch plan. AUTO-only drafts skip the MANUAL stage and MANUAL-only drafts skip the AUTO stage. If recommendations are absent or rejected, submit customer-approved customCandidates of the same family to the continuation; do not recreate the already-created structure. For every AUTO ad group, explain that Amazon creates exactly four targets after the ad group exists and record automaticTargetBidding.mode as KEEP_DEFAULT, AMAZON_SUGGESTED, CUSTOM, or DECIDE_LATER; CUSTOM requires all four official theme bids. Never model those themes as manually created targets. Every supplied nested entity requires a stable clientRef. Updating requires draftId and expectedDraftVersion; arrays merge by clientRef and remove only through removeClientRefs. When the draft is READY, call continue_workflow_draft. The server then persists the current atomic plan, created Amazon IDs, recommendation choices, and bid choice so later calls safely resume. Every returned write plan must still be shown, explicitly confirmed, and applied. Pass applyContinuation to the matching operation-specific execution tool so successful writes automatically prepare the next stage; never ask the customer for permission merely to advance. Recommendation 429 responses are recoverable and do not create a write plan. During draft collection, accept syntactically valid SKU/ASIN values without querying Inventory or Listings; production Product Ad plan preparation performs product resolution.

tools.description: Query the latest Amazon Brand Analytics search-term report for one supported marketplace: US ATVPDKIKX0DER, CA A2EUQ1WTGCTBG2, UK A1F83G8C2ARO7P, DE A1PA6795UKMFR9, FR A13V1IB3VIYZZH, IT APJ6JRA9NG5V4, ES A1RKKUPIHCS9HS, JP A1VC38T7YXB528. Returns the current-week report plus raw previousWeek (1 week earlier), sameWeekLastMonth (4 weeks earlier), and sameWeekLastQuarter (12 weeks earlier) snapshots (rank, click share, conversion share) and the latest 13 weekly rank points. Comparison snapshots are raw baselines, not calculated changes or rates. BROWSE is paginated. EXACT accepts 1 to 100 terms and FUZZY accepts one keyword; neither accepts pagination or sorting, and FUZZY returns at most the first 100 Lucene matches. searchFrequencyRank is the weekly search rank. searchVolume is weekly search volume. totalClickShare and totalConversionShare are percentages from 0 through 100, not counts or decimal fractions. Trend point weekStartDate is the week start date. supplyDemandRatio is searchVolume divided by competingListingCount (searches per competing listing), not a percentage. query.status is MATCHED when at least one item matched and NO_MATCH otherwise; inspect each item.matched for per-term results. pagination is present only for BROWSE and contains offset and limit but no total or hasMore. This is marketplace research data, not keyword-rank tracking or advertising search-term performance.

tools.name: query_advertising_bid_recommendations
tools.description: Read-only POST that returns current Amazon suggested bids and bid ranges for 1 to 100 Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, or Sponsored Display targeting items. For an existing keyword or target, provide targetingType and targetingId only. For a candidate that has not been created, first create its ad group, then provide targetingType, adGroupId, and targeting; this operation does not create the candidate. The server resolves the advertising product, Campaign, and Ad Group from synchronized data, so clients do not provide adProduct or campaignId. Compatible items in the same product, Campaign, Ad Group, and targeting type are combined into one Amazon recommendation request. Successful group responses are cached briefly and reused for identical requests. If a group is rate-limited, earlier successful groups are preserved, later groups of the same advertising product are not sent, and other advertising products continue. Retry only retryItemIndexes after retryAfterSeconds; do not immediately repeat the complete request when requestFingerprint is unchanged. Rate-limited and deliberately skipped unfinished items both retain the backward-compatible TOO_MANY_REQUESTS code; details distinguish them. Retrieves bid recommendations from Amazon Ads using the authorized advertising profile, or reuses cached recommendation results. Supports existing targets and supplied keyword or product targeting candidates that have not been created in the advertising account. This is a read-only tool: it neither creates targeting entities nor applies the returned bid. Use it when a bid decision needs Amazon's recommendation; historical CPC is not a suggested bid. Never repeat an unchanged request in the same assistant turn. Reuse successful items and the same requestFingerprint response. On TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, wait at least retryAfterSeconds and call this tool again with only retryItemIndexes.

tools.name: query_advertising_target_recommendations
tools.description: Read-only POST that returns Amazon-recommended keyword or ASIN targeting candidates before targeting entities are created. Supply exactly one source: adGroupId, or asins with adProduct. With adGroupId, the server resolves Campaign, advertising product, advertised ASINs, Sponsored Brands creative context, and Sponsored Display tactic from synchronized data. Sponsored Products supports KEYWORD and TARGET recommendations, Sponsored Brands supports KEYWORD and TARGET recommendations, and Sponsored Display supports TARGET recommendations only. Sponsored Display ASIN product recommendations require tactic T00020 because Amazon v3.3 does not support PRODUCT recommendations for T00030. TARGET currently means recommended ASIN product targets; category, brand, and audience recommendations are not included. Sponsored Products and Sponsored Brands TARGET responses can return nextToken for the next page. Pass that token back unchanged while keeping the original recommendation context. If Amazon rate-limits any page, the server does not retry and returns HTTP 429 with code TOO_MANY_REQUESTS; retain previously received items and retry only the failed page with the same nextToken. Each returned targeting object can be copied into a candidate bid-recommendation item together with the created adGroupId and targetingType, then used to create the selected target. This operation does not create or update advertising entities. Recommendations are retrieved from the Amazon Ads recommendation APIs using the authorized advertising profile and supplied context. Returned candidates are not limited to targeting entities already present in the user's advertising account. Use this tool first when the customer has not selected targeting candidates, then pass selected targeting objects to query_advertising_bid_recommendations before creation.

tools.name: query_keyword_rank_trackers
tools.description: One trackingScope per request: PARENT (default) uses parentAsin and tracks the family; CHILD uses asin and tracks only that exact variation, excluding siblings. The server resolves its parent. For tracker lists use parentAsins with PARENT or asins with CHILD. Query, ADD, RESUME, REMOVE and SET_COMPETITORS must preserve the same scope and target. Both OWN_PRODUCT and independent COMPETITOR support CHILD. For OWN_PRODUCT associations, PARENT competitorAsins are parent/standalone ASINs while CHILD competitorAsins are exact variation ASINs. includeCompetitors compares the same scope. Account capabilities and notices are returned even for empty results. Check advertisingRankTracking before interpreting advertising ranks or offering advertising tracking. False means unsupported, not a missing match; never promise advertising ranks or silently substitute organic tracking for an explicit advertising-rank request. This applies to own products, independent competitors, and associated competitors. Returns keyword rank tracking configuration across authorized stores. tools.name: query_keyword_rank_trends
tools.description: One trackingScope per request: PARENT (default) uses parentAsin and tracks the family; CHILD uses asin and tracks only that exact variation, excluding siblings. The server resolves its parent. For tracker lists use parentAsins with PARENT or asins with CHILD. Query, ADD, RESUME, REMOVE and SET_COMPETITORS must preserve the same scope and target. Both OWN_PRODUCT and independent COMPETITOR support CHILD. For OWN_PRODUCT associations, PARENT competitorAsins are parent/standalone ASINs while CHILD competitorAsins are exact variation ASINs. includeCompetitors compares the same scope. Account capabilities and notices are returned even for empty results. Check advertisingRankTracking before interpreting advertising ranks or offering advertising tracking. False means unsupported, not a missing match; never promise advertising ranks or silently substitute organic tracking for an explicit advertising-rank request. This applies to own products, independent competitors, and associated competitors. First discover tracked products and keywords with query_keyword_rank_trackers (all matching configuration is returned without pagination). For DAILY, provide one storeId, one scope-specific ASIN and 1 to 10 exact tracked keywords, plus startDate/endDate (up to 90 inclusive marketplace-local days). All requested daily points return in one response; there is no offset/limit pagination. Split more than 10 keywords into separate requests. Each day keeps the last actual observation; absent days are not synthesized. Equal-time ties use child ASIN descending, current source first, then ID descending, not best rank. RAW uses the same storeId and scope-specific ASIN with exactly one keyword, supports 31 inclusive days, and uses offset and limit (default and maximum 100) over observation points; increase offset by limit until fewer than limit points are returned. RAW preserves distinct child ASINs and prefers current records over archived copies. One product type per request: OWN_PRODUCT (default) or independent COMPETITOR. Call separately for each type; ALL and mixed selections are not supported. Competitors share account-wide marketplace/keyword quota with owned products. MCP reporting and workflow metric date ranges use yyyy-MM-dd and include both startDate and endDate, with at most 95 calendar days per range. For longer read-only reports, split into non-overlapping windows: endDate = startDate plus 94 days, capped at the requested end date; the next startDate is the previous endDate plus 1 day. Apply the same limit independently to comparison ranges. Do not average ratios such as ACOS or ROAS across windows; recompute them from summed base metrics. Do not automatically split advertising write plans or metric-based selectors; obtain a supported analysis window from the user. Keyword ranking trends have separate limits: DAILY supports up to 90 inclusive days and RAW up to 31 inclusive days. For keyword ranking trends, use these interval-specific limits when splitting read-only reports. This reporting limit does not apply to campaign scheduling dates.

tools.description: Returns sales summaries, daily sales summaries, SKU sales, or daily SKU sales for a business date range. The range is inclusive and each request may contain at most 95 calendar days. When splitting a longer range, set endDate to startDate plus 94 days, then start the next range at the previous endDate plus 1 day; a 95-day difference between startDate and endDate would contain 96 inclusive days and is invalid. MCP reporting and workflow metric date ranges use yyyy-MM-dd and include both startDate and endDate, with at most 95 calendar days per range. For longer read-only reports, split into non-overlapping windows: endDate = startDate plus 94 days, capped at the requested end date; the next startDate is the previous endDate plus 1 day. Apply the same limit independently to comparison ranges. Do not average ratios such as ACOS or ROAS across windows; recompute them from summed base metrics. Do not automatically split advertising write plans or metric-based selectors; obtain a supported analysis window from the user. Keyword ranking trends have separate limits: DAILY supports up to 90 inclusive days and RAW up to 31 inclusive days. For keyword ranking trends, use these interval-specific limits when splitting read-only reports. This reporting limit does not apply to campaign scheduling dates.

tools.name: query_sales_orders
tools.description: Returns one store's sales orders with all order items in descending purchase time. Uses a UTC start-inclusive, end-exclusive window of at most 31 days. Excludes canceled, non-Amazon and replacement orders. SKU and promotion filters select whole orders. The time window always filters purchasedAt (order purchase time), never refund or return event time. REFUND means the order currently has a refund flag in the latest synchronized data; it does not necessarily mean a full refund or a physical return. An order purchased in July and refunded in September matches a July purchase window with REFUND, but not a September purchase window. Historical results may change after later refunds are synchronized. This endpoint cannot answer which refunds or returns occurred during a period. Amounts may be estimated; amounts after promotion are not settlement proceeds. Missing prices or order currency produce null amounts. Use this endpoint for individual orders and their items; use Sales reports for aggregated sales metrics and Profit reports for profit, refunds and costs. Order amount sums are not guaranteed to reconcile with report sales or netSales. Returns no total count. Offset pagination is not a snapshot; deduplicate by storeId and orderId when collecting changing data.

flags.description: Resumes a READY AD_STRUCTURE_CREATE draft from persisted server state. This call may query Amazon Ads for keyword or ASIN candidates and suggested bids, including candidates not yet created in the account, or reuse saved recommendations. It persists workflow progress and decisions. It reconciles the last atomic plan, retains successful Amazon IDs, and prepares exactly the next Campaign, Ad Group, Product Ad, automatic-target bid, or Targeting plan. All Campaigns are prepared together, then all Ad Groups, then all Product Ads across every ad group in one multi-group plan; the Product Ad plan is completed before any targeting recommendation or bid decision can pause another structure. It never confirms or applies a write plan. For AUTO ad groups it persists the selected bid mode with the created adGroupId, synchronizes the four Amazon-created targets, obtains suggested bids when selected, and returns a separately confirmable AD_TARGETING_CHANGE plan. Partial writes retry only failed items. A 429 suggestion read includes per-target evidence; ambiguous create results require reconciliation and are never retried. For MANUAL ad groups without supplied positive targeting, it waits until Product Ads exist, persists Amazon candidates only for the recorded KEYWORD or ASIN TARGET family, accepts customer selection by candidateRef, obtains suggested or custom bids, accepts explicit customCandidates when recommendations are absent or rejected, and prepares separately confirmable Targeting plans. It accepts at most 100 selected candidates per ad group and reuses the exact suggested bids already shown to the customer. Once every manual decision is ready, it combines all MANUAL positive targeting groups into one batch plan, then combines all configured negative targeting across AUTO and MANUAL groups into one separate batch plan. AUTO-only drafts skip MANUAL processing and MANUAL-only drafts skip AUTO processing. When a plan is returned, pass applyContinuation unchanged to the matching operation-specific execution tool so a successful write automatically returns the next stage preview without asking the customer to advance. After an AUTO bid write, immediately present the returned MANUAL targeting preview or selection action in the same response when manual groups remain.

Collect the Sponsored Products Campaign/Ad Group/Product Ad structure and any targeting the customer already supplied. One MANUAL ad group can contain only one positive targeting family: KEYWORD or ASIN TARGET. If positive targeting is omitted, collect manualTargetingFamily=KEYWORD|TARGET before execution. If the customer wants both, model separate manual Campaign/Ad Group structures from the start and assign one family to each; never put both into one ad group. Every ad group needs a negative-targeting decision: supplied allowed negative items automatically record negativeTargetingMode=CONFIGURED; when none are supplied, recommend negatives and ask the customer to choose CONFIGURED or NONE. AUTO permits both negative keywords and negative ASINs; a MANUAL KEYWORD group permits only negative keywords, and a MANUAL TARGET group permits only negative ASINs. Continuation prepares all Campaigns together, then all Ad Groups, then all Product Ads across every ad group in one multi-group plan before any AUTO bid decision or MANUAL recommendation can pause the draft. After all Product Ads exist, continuation queries and persists Amazon recommendations only for each manual ad group's recorded family, asks the customer to choose up to 100 candidates, obtains suggested or custom bids, then combines all ready MANUAL positive targeting into one Targeting batch plan. It subsequently combines every configured negative targeting item across AUTO and MANUAL structures into one separate negative Targeting batch plan. AUTO-only drafts skip the MANUAL stage and MANUAL-only drafts skip the AUTO stage. If recommendations are absent or rejected, submit customer-approved customCandidates of the same family to the continuation; do not recreate the already-created structure. For every AUTO ad group, explain that Amazon creates exactly four targets after the ad group exists and record automaticTargetBidding.mode as KEEP_DEFAULT, AMAZON_SUGGESTED, CUSTOM, or DECIDE_LATER; CUSTOM requires all four official theme bids. Never model those themes as manually created targets. Every supplied nested entity requires a stable clientRef. Updating requires draftId and expectedDraftVersion; arrays merge by clientRef and remove only through removeClientRefs. When the draft is READY, call continue_workflow_draft. The server then persists the current atomic plan, created Amazon IDs, recommendation choices, and bid choice so later calls safely resume. Every returned write plan must still be shown, explicitly confirmed, and applied. Pass applyContinuation to the matching operation-specific execution tool so successful writes automatically prepare the next stage; never ask the customer for permission merely to advance. Recommendation 429 responses are recoverable and do not create a write plan. During draft collection, accept syntactically valid SKU/ASIN values without querying Inventory or Listings; production Product Ad plan preparation performs product resolution.

flags.description: Read-only POST that returns current Amazon suggested bids and bid ranges for 1 to 100 Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, or Sponsored Display targeting items. For an existing keyword or target, provide targetingType and targetingId only. For a candidate that has not been created, first create its ad group, then provide targetingType, adGroupId, and targeting; this operation does not create the candidate. The server resolves the advertising product, Campaign, and Ad Group from synchronized data, so clients do not provide adProduct or campaignId. Compatible items in the same product, Campaign, Ad Group, and targeting type are combined into one Amazon recommendation request. Successful group responses are cached briefly and reused for identical requests. If a group is rate-limited, earlier successful groups are preserved, later groups of the same advertising product are not sent, and other advertising products continue. Retry only retryItemIndexes after retryAfterSeconds; do not immediately repeat the complete request when requestFingerprint is unchanged. Rate-limited and deliberately skipped unfinished items both retain the backward-compatible TOO_MANY_REQUESTS code; details distinguish them. Retrieves bid recommendations from Amazon Ads using the authorized advertising profile, or reuses cached recommendation results. Supports existing targets and supplied keyword or product targeting candidates that have not been created in the advertising account. This is a read-only tool: it neither creates targeting entities nor applies the returned bid. Use it when a bid decision needs Amazon's recommendation; historical CPC is not a suggested bid. Never repeat an unchanged request in the same assistant turn. Reuse successful items and the same requestFingerprint response. On TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, wait at least retryAfterSeconds and call this tool again with only retryItemIndexes.

flags.description: Look up natural search terms for a marketplace ASIN. The ASIN may be a variation parent, child, or standalone product; callers do not need to know its type. For a parent, returns child ASINs and each child's available search-term count; ask which child the user means, then call this same tool for that child. For a child or standalone ASIN, SUMMARY (default) returns the first 100 terms in PC order; FULL returns the complete available list. If the user explicitly requests all terms, use FULL on the first call for the selected child. naturalIdx is this ASIN's natural rank; searchFrequencyRank is the keyword's ABA weekly search rank. searchVolume is weekly search volume. This tool does not return advertising bids or keyword trends; use an ABA tool for a selected keyword's weekly trend. If variation lookup is unavailable, variationType is UNKNOWN, not a claim that the ASIN is standalone.

flags.description: One trackingScope per request: PARENT (default) uses parentAsin and tracks the family; CHILD uses asin and tracks only that exact variation, excluding siblings. The server resolves its parent. For tracker lists use parentAsins with PARENT or asins with CHILD. Query, ADD, RESUME, REMOVE and SET_COMPETITORS must preserve the same scope and target. Both OWN_PRODUCT and independent COMPETITOR support CHILD. For OWN_PRODUCT associations, PARENT competitorAsins are parent/standalone ASINs while CHILD competitorAsins are exact variation ASINs. includeCompetitors compares the same scope. Account capabilities and notices are returned even for empty results. Check advertisingRankTracking before interpreting advertising ranks or offering advertising tracking. False means unsupported, not a missing match; never promise advertising ranks or silently substitute organic tracking for an explicit advertising-rank request. This applies to own products, independent competitors, and associated competitors. Returns keyword rank tracking configuration across authorized stores. Groups top-level items by storeId and the selected tracking target with nested keywords, and may include PENDING_KEYWORDS parents. Each tracking record has a stable trackingId and its own ACTIVE or PAUSED state. PAUSED means the system stopped tracking due to package expiry or restrictions; it is not a customer pause action. Restore it with RESUME only when package access and quota permit. Returns all matching configuration without pagination. Product title and imageUrl are included when available. Latest rankings are not included; use query_keyword_rank_trends with storeId, parentAsin and keywords to retrieve rankings. This tool does not return Search Volume or calculate rank changes. Query query_account_usages with resources=[KEYWORD_RANK_TRACKING_KEYWORDS] for account quota; list counts are not quota usage. One product type per request: OWN_PRODUCT (default) or independent COMPETITOR. Call separately for each type; ALL and mixed selections are not supported. Competitors share account-wide marketplace/keyword quota with owned products. To create tracking use prepare_keyword_rank_tracking_creation; to resume or archive existing keywords use prepare_keyword_rank_tracking_changes; to replace associated competitors use prepare_keyword_rank_competitor_replacement. Follow each published schema and obtain explicit customer confirmation before its matching apply tool. Preserve the returned trackingScope: PARENT uses parentAsin; CHILD uses asin. Never substitute the parent when a customer requests one child.

First discover tracked products and keywords with query_keyword_rank_trackers (all matching configuration is returned without pagination). For DAILY, provide one storeId, one scope-specific ASIN and 1 to 10 exact tracked keywords, plus startDate/endDate (up to 90 inclusive marketplace-local days). All requested daily points return in one response; there is no offset/limit pagination. Split more than 10 keywords into separate requests. Each day keeps the last actual observation; absent days are not synthesized. Equal-time ties use child ASIN descending, current source first, then ID descending, not best rank. RAW uses the same storeId and scope-specific ASIN with exactly one keyword, supports 31 inclusive days, and uses offset and limit (default and maximum 100) over observation points; increase offset by limit until fewer than limit points are returned. RAW preserves distinct child ASINs and prefers current records over archived copies. One product type per request: OWN_PRODUCT (default) or independent COMPETITOR. Call separately for each type; ALL and mixed selections are not supported. Competitors share account-wide marketplace/keyword quota with owned products. MCP reporting and workflow metric date ranges use yyyy-MM-dd and include both startDate and endDate, with at most 95 calendar days per range. For longer read-only reports, split into non-overlapping windows: endDate = startDate plus 94 days, capped at the requested end date; the next startDate is the previous endDate plus 1 day. Apply the same limit independently to comparison ranges. Do not average ratios such as ACOS or ROAS across windows; recompute them from summed base metrics. Do not automatically split advertising write plans or metric-based selectors; obtain a supported analysis window from the user. Keyword ranking trends have separate limits: DAILY supports up to 90 inclusive days and RAW up to 31 inclusive days. For keyword ranking trends, use these interval-specific limits when splitting read-only reports. This reporting limit does not apply to campaign scheduling dates.

flags.description: Returns one store's sales orders with all order items in descending purchase time. Uses a UTC start-inclusive, end-exclusive window of at most 31 days. Excludes canceled, non-Amazon and replacement orders. SKU and promotion filters select whole orders. The time window always filters purchasedAt (order purchase time), never refund or return event time. REFUND means the order currently has a refund flag in the latest synchronized data; it does not necessarily mean a full refund or a physical return. An order purchased in July and refunded in September matches a July purchase window with REFUND, but not a September purchase window. Historical results may change after later refunds are synchronized. This endpoint cannot answer which refunds or returns occurred during a period. Amounts may be estimated; amounts after promotion are not settlement proceeds. Missing prices or order currency produce null amounts. Use this endpoint for individual orders and their items; use Sales reports for aggregated sales metrics and Profit reports for profit, refunds and costs. Order amount sums are not guaranteed to reconcile with report sales or netSales. Returns no total count. Offset pagination is not a snapshot; deduplicate by storeId and orderId when collecting changing data.
